findings.evidence: "Trigger guidance only in the body is a D4 finding. The body is invisible until the skill has already triggered." repeats rubric.md D4 ("Never accept 'when to use' guidance that exists only in the body") and failure pattern 7; line 72 ("NEVER reward polish, length or self-praise") likewise repeats the rubric scoring rule "Never credit a claim the skill makes about itself"
findings.fix: The rubric is always read in full in step 1, so drop the copies: delete the line-68 gotcha and cut line 72 down to the one part the rubric lacks ("a 43-line skill can outperform a 500-line one"). Use the freed lines for protocol-only knowledge.

findings.evidence: The Gotchas list has no attribution rule. The protection that credits ("## Attribution", "based on", "adapted from", upstream links) never count against any dimension exists only in references/judge-prompt.md (rule 5), and step 3 forbids reading that file unless skill-judge is the target, so direct-use runs never see it
findings.fix: Add a gotcha: "- **Attribution is never a deduction.** Lines that credit an author, upstream source, inspiration or license (## Attribution, ## Credits, 'based on', 'adapted from', upstream links) do not count against D1 or any other dimension. When a credit sits in `description`, the fix moves it to the end of the body or to README.md and never deletes it."

findings.evidence: All 11 evals judge a single fixture file (SKILL.md.txt, ship-note.md, triage-agent.md). None gives a full skill directory with evals/ or scripts/, so step 3 (reading evals/evals.json and trigger-queries.json for D7, and the 'scripts/ exists but tests/skills/<name>/ was not checked' branch with its 5/5/5 allocation) is never exercised
findings.fix: Add an evals/files/<name>/ fixture directory that has SKILL.md.txt, scripts/ and evals/ but no matching tests/skills/<name>/. Add an eval asserting that D7 keeps the 5/5/5 split, that no point is deducted for the unseen smoke test, and that a D7 finding states the limit.

findings.evidence: "Then classify each H2 section for D1 and weight it by line count: the D1 ratio is in lines, not sections." The step does not say how the line ratio maps to the rubric's 0-20 bands, or how to count frontmatter and the H1 preamble, so two judges can compute the same ratio and still pick different bands
findings.fix: Append to step 4: "Count body lines only (exclude frontmatter). Let the preamble before the first H2 count as one section. A ratio that meets the rubric's good ratio (>70% expert, <10% redundant) scores 16-20. Score 11-15 when redundant is 10-20%, and 6-10 when redundant exceeds 20%, unless a red flag caps it at 5."
